Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — Uzbekistan and Polish company Mlekovita have discussed prospects for joint projects in the dairy industry, the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade of Uzbekistan said. The cooperation opportunities were discussed at a meeting between Deputy Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Ibrahim Ergashev and Mlekovita Management Board Chairman Dariusz Sapinski. The talks covered potential joint investment and production projects, as well as arrangements for exporting dairy products.

400.title: Europe could save 40% on electricity costs if solar and batteries ‘work in harmony’ | Framing Analysis
400.summary: Europe could save 40% on electricity costs if solar and batteries ‘work in harmony’ Tap a highlight to see why it matters.
400.body: Europe could save 40% on electricity costs if solar and batteries ‘work in harmony’ Tap a highlight to see why it matters. First highlight 1 finding See it marked on euronews.com Europe could save 40 per cent on electricity costs thanks to solar and batteries – but only if the complimentary technologies are deployed correctly.Solar has rapidly become a leader in clean energy, helping the world transition away from polluting fossil fuels and cushioning households from volatile oil and gas price spikes. A new report launched during the UN COP31 climate summit has revealed just how much this combination can shape total electricity costs in Europe.Will Europe’s solar and battery boom pay off? The report, from the Schneider Electric Research Institute (SERI), modelled 40,500 scenarios across different combinations of solar, battery and grid costs to identify whether the rise of distributed energy resources (DERs) will ultimately raise or lower electricity costs overall.

500.title: Fireworks AI Breach Exposes Wider Risks in Enterprise Security
500.summary: The U.K.'s fireworks celebrations last week may be behind us, but a breach at AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI has kept the focus this week on a different kind of explosive fallout in the form of security risks in enterprise AI supply chains.
500.body: The U.K.'s fireworks celebrations last week may be behind us, but a breach at AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI has kept the focus this week on a different kind of explosive fallout in the form of security risks in enterprise AI supply chains. The incident exposed customer datasets, incomplete model weights and sensitive account information through a third-party provider, once again raising questions about the security of the infrastructure supporting enterprise AI services. For me, the Fireworks AI breach points to a wider challenge around customer trust and other developments this week show how broadly that challenge applies, with a number of developments suggesting implications for how enterprises protect customer information and maintain confidence in their services.
